titleStmt.title: The Emergence of Single Neurons in Clinical Neurology
titleStmt.author: Cash
Hochberg

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: The Emergence of Single Neurons in Clinical Neurology

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the place of single-neuron activity in clinical neurology, neurosurgery and psychiatry
span.quote: Single neuron actions and interactions are the sine qua non of brain function, and nearly all diseases and injuries of the central nervous system trace their clinical sequelae to neuronal dysfunction or failure. Remarkably, discussion of neuronal activity is largely absent in clinical neuroscience.

span.label: why single-neuron activity is missing from clinical practice, and what is now making it available
span.quote: This state of affairs is not surprising for many reasons. Arguably, much of the pathology that is seen in routine clinical practice such as stroke, trauma, inflammation, infection, and tumors, are not recognized or considered to be diseases of the individual neuron. Even motor neuron disease, demyelinating diseases, and other neurodegenerative diseases are not, in toto , diseases of an individual neuron; they are manifestations of a more widespread pathology.

span.label: documents an absence in a literature, explains it by the absence of an instrument, and surveys the technologies now removing the constraint
span.quote: The only references to single neuron activity and action potentials in searching through classic textbooks of neurology (e.g. Adams and Victor's 8 th edition, Ropper and Brown, eds. ( Ropper, AH; Brown, RJ; Brown, 2005 )) are related to peripheral nerves.

span.label: prediction
span.quote: Using direct interfaces with the nervous system, millisecond-scale information will soon be extracted from single neurons in clinical environments, supporting personalized treatment of neurologic and psychiatric disease.

span.label: single-neuron recording in clinical neurology
span.quote: Single neuron actions and interactions are the sine qua non of brain function, and nearly all diseases and injuries of the central nervous system trace their clinical sequelae to neuronal dysfunction or failure.

span.label: review
span.quote: In this review we focus on single neuronal activity in restoring communication and motor control in patients suffering from devastating neurological injuries.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Clinical neglect of the single neuron is explained by the prior unavailability of technology able to target or measure small groups of neurons
span.quote: Perhaps even more important to the general clinical neglect of the single neuron is the previous absence of relevant technology.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Propofol produces unconsciousness by phase-locking cortical neurons to local slow oscillations that are out of phase across regions, fragmenting long-range cortical communication
span.quote: Single unit recordings during loss of consciousness demonstrated that cortical neurons become phase-locked to local slow oscillations, but are out of phase with distant cortical areas, producing a fragmented network in which long-range cortical communication is disrupted.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Loss of dopamine erodes the separation normally maintained between basal ganglia subcircuits, so circuit elements merge into larger hypersynchronised networks that drive motor cortical synchrony
span.quote: When that dopaminergically maintained separation erodes circuit elements form larger, hypersynchronized networks

span.label: the absence is attributed to instrument resolution: MRI, EEG and MEG cannot resolve activity at the scale of the action potential
span.quote: While the spatial resolution of modern structural and functional MRI, the temporal sensitivity of electroencephalography (EEG) or magnetoencephalography (MEG) and the exploding capabilities of genetics and proteomics are remarkable, they are not capable of resolving neuronal activity at its most fundamental scale of the action potential and its firing rates or patterns.

span.label: and to the absence of any intervention that could target small groups of neurons, let alone one
span.quote: Perhaps even more important to the general clinical neglect of the single neuron is the previous absence of relevant technology. Until recently there were essentially no diagnostic examinations or therapeutic interventions that could target modest groups of neurons let alone single neurons.

span.label: and to the nature of the pathology: stroke, trauma, tumours are not diseases of an individual neuron
span.quote: This state of affairs is not surprising for many reasons. Arguably, much of the pathology that is seen in routine clinical practice such as stroke, trauma, inflammation, infection, and tumors, are not recognized or considered to be diseases of the individual neuron. Even motor neuron disease, demyelinating diseases, and other neurodegenerative diseases are not, in toto , diseases of an individual neuron; they are manifestations of a more widespread pathology.

span.label: and to the confinement of the relevant physiology to animal models in a small subset of laboratories
span.quote: Also until recently, only in animal models have the physiologic activities of small populations of individual neurons been examined, and this by only a relatively small subset of laboratories.

span.label: propofol unconsciousness explained mechanistically: neurons phase-lock to local slow oscillations but fall out of phase with distant cortex, fragmenting the network
span.quote: Single unit recordings during loss of consciousness demonstrated that cortical neurons become phase-locked to local slow oscillations, but are out of phase with distant cortical areas, producing a fragmented network in which long-range cortical communication is disrupted.

span.label: in Parkinson's, dopaminergic loss is hypothesised to erode the separation between basal ganglia subcircuits, which then hypersynchronise
span.quote: This synchronization is hypothesized to relate to dopaminergic loss which, normally, maintains separation between basal ganglia subcircuits. When that dopaminergically maintained separation erodes circuit elements form larger, hypersynchronized networks

span.label: single-unit firing patterns mark the boundaries of the STN and globus pallidus as the electrode advances, the one routine clinical use
span.quote: For example, the boundaries of the subthalamic nucleus (STN) or globus pallidus internus can be determined based on firing rates and patterns which change as the electrode tip traverses a given region

span.label: Much relevant work on miniaturised and wireless implanted recording is acknowledged as outside the review's scope.
span.note: what this limits: the technological coverage of the review: THERE ARE MANY IMPORTANT RESEARCH ENDEAVORS IN THIS FIELD WHICH ARE BEYOND THE SCOPE OF THIS REVIEW
span.quote: note there are many important research endeavors in this field which are beyond the scope of this review

span.label: The cognitive-neuroscience literature on human single units is only sampled, not covered.
span.note: what this limits: the cognitive-neuroscience coverage: A COMPLETE EXPLORATION OF THESE MYRIAD TOPICS IS BEYOND THE SCOPE OF THIS REVIEW
span.quote: A complete exploration of these myriad topics is beyond the scope of this review

span.label: The cognitive single-unit findings surveyed are conceded to have no immediate clinical application.
span.note: what this limits: clinical application specifically: THESE FINDINGS ARE INDEED NOT YET OF IMMEDIATE CLINICAL RELEVANCE
span.quote: While these findings are indeed not yet of immediate clinical relevance they are crucial in gaining a deeper understanding of brain function.

span.label: the relationship between any animal model of epilepsy and human epilepsy is unclear, unlike the primate-human motor cortex case
span.note: what this limits: any transfer from animal epilepsy models: UNLIKE THE MOTOR PROSTHESIS APPROACH IN WHICH THE SIMILARITY BETWEEN NONHUMAN PRIMATE M1 AND HUMAN M1 IS EVIDENT, THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN ANY GIVEN ANIMAL MODEL and human epilepsy is unclear
span.quote: Unlike the motor prosthesis approach in which the similarity between nonhuman primate M1 and human M1 is evident in the underlying anatomy (and, as now being demonstrated, physiology), the relationship between any given animal model of epilepsy and the various forms of human epilepsy is unclear.

span.label: the details of single-neuron activity in the seizure focus itself remain poorly understood
span.note: what this limits: claims about the seizure focus itself: THE DETAILS OF SINGLE NEURON ACTIVITY IN THE FOCUS remain poorly understood
span.quote: In fact, the details of single neuron activity in the “focus

span.label: decades of seizure-prediction work has produced no clinically usable algorithm
span.note: what this limits: every seizure-prediction method reviewed: NONE HAS LED TO A CLINICALLY USEABLE OR COMMERCIALLY SUCCESSFUL PREDICTIVE ALGORITHM
span.quote: While these methods have recently moved toward devices and commercially supported clinical trials ( Cook et al., 2013 ) none has led to a clinically useable or commercially successful predictive algorithm

span.label: the spiking activity underlying most anaesthetic EEG signatures is simply not known
span.note: what this limits: the spiking basis of anaesthetic EEG patterns: THE SPIKE (ACTION POTENTIAL) ACTIVITY UNDERLYING MANY OF THESE PATTERNS IS NOT KNOWN, WITH THE EXCEPTION OF SLOW OSCILLATIONS DURING PROPOFOL INDUCED ANESTHESIA
span.quote: The spike (action potential) activity underlying many of these patterns is not known, with the exception of slow oscillations during propofol induced anesthesia, described below.

span.label: animal brains are too small to study large-scale cortical relationships, and human scalp EEG has too little spatial resolution - neither end of the scale is available
span.note: what this limits: large-scale cortical claims from either source: THE SMALL SIZE OF THE BRAIN IN THE ANIMAL MODELS HAS PREVENTED MUCH ANALYSIS OF LARGE-SCALE RELATIONSHIPS ACROSS THE CORTEX, AND HUMAN STUDIES OF SCALP EEG PROVIDE LITTLE SPATIAL RESOLUTION
span.quote: However, the small size of the brain in the animal models (e.g. rodents and cats) has prevented much analysis of large-scale relationships across the cortex, and human studies of scalp EEG provide little spatial resolution.

span.label: the cognitive single-unit findings are not yet of immediate clinical relevance, stated plainly
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 2 - not yet of immediate clinical relevance
span.quote: While these findings are indeed not yet of immediate clinical relevance they are crucial in gaining a deeper understanding of brain function. In addition, understanding the neural correlates of these various processes sets an essential foundation for the advanced treatment of cognitive deficits in both neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric diseases.

span.label: data volumes already exceed what current techniques can extract meaning from
span.note: what this limits: what can be extracted from the recordings at all: THIS MUCH NEURAL DATA CHALLENGES OUR COMPUTATIONAL CAPABILITIES AND, ESSENTIALLY, OUR TECHNIQUES FOR EXTRACTING MEANINGFUL INFORMATION FROM THIS HIGH DIMENSIONAL DATA SET
span.quote: Beyond its simple storage, this much neural data challenges our computational capabilities and, essentially, our techniques for extracting meaningful information from this high dimensional data set.

span.label: after forty years single-unit physiology is still a small component of practice
span.note: what this limits: the clinical uptake claim: SINGLE UNIT PHYSIOLOGY IS STILL A SMALL COMPONENT OF NEUROLOGIC AND PSYCHIATRIC PRACTICE, after A MORE THAN 40-YEAR HISTORY
span.quote: Although there is a more than 40-year history of considering cerebral action potentials in clinical thinking, single unit physiology is still a small component of neurologic and psychiatric practice.

span.label: the encoding of movement in M1, transferred to human brain-computer interfaces - the transfer the paper says IS licensed, because the anatomy is evidently similar
span.quote: Largely through research with non-human primates, a foundation was developed for understanding the anatomic and functional organization of primary motor cortex and other motor-related areas ( Evarts, 1966 , 1967 , 1968b , 1968a ; Fetz, 1969 ; DeLong, 1971 ; DeLong and Strick, 1974 ; Tanji and Evarts, 1976 ; Weinrich and Wise, 1982 ; Georgopoulos et al., 1982 , 1984 , 1989 ; Wise, 1985 , 1993 ; Donoghue, 1985 ; DeLong et al., 1986 ; Kettner et al., 1988 ; Schwartz et al., 1988 ; Caminiti et al., 1990 ; Sanes et al., 1990 ; Kalaska and Crammond, 1992 ; Ashe and Georgopoulos, 1994 ; Donoghue and Sanes, 1994 ; Fu et al., 1995 ; Taira et al., 1996 ; Scott and Kalaska, 1997 ; Shen and Alexander, 1997 ; Hatsopoulos et al., 1998 ; Wise et al., 1998 ; Sergio and Kalaska, 1998 ; Kakei et al., 1999 ; Moran and Schwartz, 1999 ; Gandolfo et al., 2000 ; Sanes and Donoghue, 2000 ; Ajemian et al., 2000 ; Li et al., 2001 ; Todorov and Jordan, 2002 ; Paz et al., 2003 ; Kemere et al., 2004 ; Paninski et al., 2004a , 2004b ; Paz and Vaadia, 2004 ; Churchland et al., 2006 ; Wu and Hatsopoulos, 2006 ; Churchland and Shenoy, 2007 ; Graziano, 2011 ; Oby et al., 2013 ; Barrese et al., 2013 ). This research demonstrated that information about many aspects of movement could be extracted from the activities of individual neurons.

span.label: the transfer the paper says is NOT licensed, because the correspondence to human epilepsy is unclear
span.quote: Unlike the motor prosthesis approach in which the similarity between nonhuman primate M1 and human M1 is evident in the underlying anatomy (and, as now being demonstrated, physiology), the relationship between any given animal model of epilepsy and the various forms of human epilepsy is unclear.

span.label: clustering algorithms, dimensionality reduction and point-process methods, imported to make terabyte-scale spike data tractable
span.quote: First amongst these are new methods for extracting spiking information from large data sets. These ‘clustering’ algorithms are now available in a variety of different forms with optimization for high speed (essentially real-time) and for working with particularly large data sets.

span.label: single unit here means an isolated action potential train from one neuron, explicitly contrasted with the averaged multineuron signals of EEG and ECoG
span.quote: While the spatial resolution of modern structural and functional MRI, the temporal sensitivity of electroencephalography (EEG) or magnetoencephalography (MEG) and the exploding capabilities of genetics and proteomics are remarkable, they are not capable of resolving neuronal activity at its most fundamental scale of the action potential and its firing rates or patterns.

span.label: gold standard is used for single-unit recording in BASIC neurophysiology, in a paper arguing it is absent from clinical practice - the standard and the practice are different communities
span.quote: The study of single neurons, action potentials, and the activity of small ensembles of individual neurons have long been the gold standard for research and understanding in basic systems neurophysiology.

span.label: hypersynchrony, as a framing of epilepsy, is said to be accurate at a superficial level and to break down under finer measurement - a claim whose truth depends on resolution
span.quote: Nonetheless, the combined research using microelectrode and macroelectrode arrays has challenged the canonical framing of epilepsy as solely a disorder of hypersynchrony and imbalanced inhibition and excitation, which may be accurate at a superficial level but breaks down under more detailed mechanistic study.

span.label: model, for epilepsy, is explicitly weaker than model for motor cortex: the primate-human M1 similarity is evident where the epilepsy correspondence is unclear
span.quote: Unlike the motor prosthesis approach in which the similarity between nonhuman primate M1 and human M1 is evident in the underlying anatomy (and, as now being demonstrated, physiology), the relationship between any given animal model of epilepsy and the various forms of human epilepsy is unclear.

span.label: claim_type: critique

span.quote: Single neuron actions and interactions are the sine qua non of brain function, and nearly all diseases and injuries of the central nervous system trace their clinical sequelae to neuronal dysfunction or failure. Remarkably, discussion of neuronal activity is largely absent in clinical neuroscience.

span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: single-neuron recording in clinical neurology — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Readers of this journal will hopefully forgive us for feeling the need to state what is obvious to any student of neuroscience – the activity of single neurons, the action potential in particular, is a central component of normal brain function. Yet this bedrock fact has remarkably little outward presence in the daily practice of clinical neurology, neurosurgery, or psychiatry.

span.label: critiques → clinical neurology, neurosurgery and psychiatry, for the absence of single-neuron thinking
span.quote: Single neuron actions and interactions are the sine qua non of brain function, and nearly all diseases and injuries of the central nervous system trace their clinical sequelae to neuronal dysfunction or failure. Remarkably, discussion of neuronal activity is largely absent in clinical neuroscience.

span.label: qualifies → the canonical framing of epilepsy as a disorder of hypersynchrony and imbalanced excitation and inhibition
span.quote: Nonetheless, the combined research using microelectrode and macroelectrode arrays has challenged the canonical framing of epilepsy as solely a disorder of hypersynchrony and imbalanced inhibition and excitation, which may be accurate at a superficial level but breaks down under more detailed mechanistic study.

span.label: supports → the use of intraoperative single-unit recording to localise DBS electrodes
span.quote: In fact, this may be the best example of using single neuron activity in direct support of clinical activity.

span.label: supports → slow-oscillation phase-locking as a mechanism of propofol-induced loss of consciousness

span.label: cites → Gelbard-Sagiv et al. on hippocampal reactivation during free recall - a paper independently tagged in this corpus
span.quote: For example, hippocampal neuronal reactivation has been demonstrated during free recall ( Gelbard-Sagiv et al., 2008 ) and spatial recall tasks

span.label: single neuron —same-as→ single unit
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — used interchangeably throughout; the second is the recorded proxy for the first, which is why the weight is not 1.0

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · propofol —causes→ slow oscillations
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span named neither the drug nor the oscillation by the edge's own terms. This sentence names both and states the dependence - the EEG under propofol 'is DOMINATED BY low frequency, high power slow oscillations'. — strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: Single unit recordings during loss of consciousness demonstrated that cortical neurons become phase-locked to local slow oscillations, but are out of phase with distant cortical areas, producing a fragmented network in which long-range cortical communication is disrupted.

span.label: propofol —causes→ slow oscillations
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — RE-GROUNDS Cash2015-the-emergence-of-single-neurons-in-clinical[4]: the old span named ONE endpoint.
span.quote: The EEG under propofol general anesthesia is dominated by low frequency, high power slow oscillations (<1 Hz), increased gamma power, and a ~10 Hz alpha oscillation in frontal channels ( Murphy et al., 2011 ; Cimenser et al., 2011 ; Purdon et al., 2013 ).

span.label: Despite being foundational to brain function, single-neuron activity has almost no presence in everyday clinical neurology, neurosurgery or psychiatry.
span.quote: Yet this bedrock fact has remarkably little outward presence in the daily practice of clinical neurology, neurosurgery, or psychiatry.

span.label: The dominant clinical measurement modalities cannot resolve activity at the scale of the action potential, which the review identifies as the core gap.
span.quote: While the spatial resolution of modern structural and functional MRI, the temporal sensitivity of electroencephalography (EEG) or magnetoencephalography (MEG) and the exploding capabilities of genetics and proteomics are remarkable, they are not capable of resolving neuronal activity at its most fundamental scale of the action potential and its firing rates or patterns.

span.label: Even after four decades of relevant recordings, single-unit physiology remains a marginal component of neurological and psychiatric practice.
span.quote: Although there is a more than 40-year history of considering cerebral action potentials in clinical thinking, single unit physiology is still a small component of neurologic and psychiatric practice.

span.label: Microelectrode and macroelectrode array work has undermined the standard account of epilepsy as purely a disorder of hypersynchrony and excitation-inhibition imbalance.
span.quote: Nonetheless, the combined research using microelectrode and macroelectrode arrays has challenged the canonical framing of epilepsy as solely a disorder of hypersynchrony and imbalanced inhibition and excitation, which may be accurate at a superficial level but breaks down under more detailed mechanistic study.

span.label: Intraoperative single-unit recording to localise basal ganglia targets during DBS is, in the authors' judgement, the clearest existing clinical use of single-neuron activity.
span.quote: In fact, this may be the best example of using single neuron activity in direct support of clinical activity.

span.label: Firing rates and patterns are used to identify the boundaries of the subthalamic nucleus and globus pallidus internus as the electrode advances.
span.quote: For example, the boundaries of the subthalamic nucleus (STN) or globus pallidus internus can be determined based on firing rates and patterns which change as the electrode tip traverses a given region

span.label: Intracortical arrays implanted from 2004 onward let people with tetraplegia produce 2D cursor movement and simple robotic control directly from cortical spiking.
span.quote: The first implantation of a system for recording single unit activity was performed in 2004 and soon afterwards, the first intracortically directed two-dimensional (2D) cursor movements and simple robotic control were accomplished by people with tetraplegia using an intracortical brain computer interface

span.label: Human single-unit studies show that individual neurons in higher-order cortex are selectively tuned to complex stimuli, supporting sparse coding.
span.quote: multiple studies now indicate that individual neurons in higher order cortices maintain tuning properties or specificity for complex stimuli

span.label: discussion of neuronal activity is largely absent from clinical neuroscience

Remarkably, discussion of neuronal activity is largely absent in clinical neuroscience.

span.quote: Waves which are often portrayed as homogenous in their effects and spatial spread are, in fact, more heterogeneous in spatial representation and their involvement of individual neurons.
